exposure: Enhanced Recovery after Caesarean Surgery (ERACS) method
cohort: The study included 60 mothers (30 in the ERACS group and 30 in the non-ERACS group) undergoing Caesarean section.
finding: ERACS was effective in reducing postoperative pain but ineffective for accelerating the onset of colostrum excretion.
mod_finding: The ERACS method, a specific technique for Caesarean section, was found to be effective in reducing postoperative pain but did not accelerate the onset of colostrum excretion compared to the non-ERACS method.
